guideTitle: 6 Best Electric Snow Shovels Under $300 in 2026
metaTitle: Best Electric Snow Shovels Under $300 in 2026
metaDescription: Six stronger cordless electric snow shovels compared, from a wheeled 16 inch brushless model to lightweight 12 inch units for decks, steps and driveways.
introParagraphs: A bigger budget lets you stop asking whether a snow shovel is good enough and start asking how much of the job it can take over. The picks here are the strongest cordless units in the electric snow shovel class: brushless motors, wider paths, deeper passes and in some cases wheels to carry the weight. They are still shovels, not blowers, but the gap is narrower than you might expect.

That shift changes the questions worth asking. How deep is the pass? Does the tool roll on wheels or do you carry its weight? Does the kit include batteries, or do you buy those separately? One pick, the EGO, ships as a bare tool with no battery or charger, which is excellent news if you already own the matching battery platform and costly news if you do not.

We evaluated these from published specs and patterns in buyer feedback, not hands-on testing. Treat throw distances and clearing claims as best-case numbers on light, fluffy snow. Wet snow cuts them noticeably, and the more powerful the tool, the more the fact that you still have to push it matters.

products.name: VOLTASK 48V 16 Inch Electric Snow Shovel with Wheels
products.description:
The 48V VOLTASK is the largest and strongest tool in the guide. A 1200W brushless motor spins a 2000 RPM auger, and the cut is 16 inches wide and 8 inches deep in one pass, a step up from the 12 to 14 inch shovels at lower budgets. Specialized wheels and an adjustable support plate help it glide over paved surfaces instead of making you carry the weight.

The wheels change how it feels to use. You push rather than lift, which spares your arms and back on a long driveway. The directional plate lets you steer where the snow goes. The tradeoffs are a larger footprint and more bulk to store, and the listing is silent on battery count and runtime in the text we saw, so confirm what is in the box.

Compared with the VOLTASK 24V 13 inch, it clears a much wider, deeper path and rolls. Compared with the BAOPROLEI, it digs deeper but includes fewer stated batteries. It is the pick for a long driveway where capacity and effort savings matter more than storage.
products.bestFor: Longer driveways where wheels and depth reduce effort.

1200W brushless motor with a 2000 RPM auger
Wheels let you push instead of carry
Adjustable support plate suits paved surfaces
cons: Largest footprint of the six to store

products.name: BAOPROLEI 40V Brushless Cordless Snow Shovel, 13 Inch
products.description:
The BAOPROLEI answers the question every cordless snow tool asks: what happens when the battery dies? It ships with three 40V 4.0Ah lithium-ion batteries and a charger, so you can rotate packs through a full driveway or a second storm. The body weighs about 12 pounds and uses a premium comfort-grip handle.

A 13 inch brushless tool is not the widest, but it moves at a steady pace and the three-battery bundle is unmatched in this list. The brand name is not well known, and the listing says little about throw distance or exact clearing depth, so look at recent buyer feedback and confirm those details.

Compared with the VOLTASK 48V, it clears a narrower path but with far more battery on hand. Compared with the Yardzpo, it has more batteries and less stated reach. If runtime is your main worry, this is the safest bet in the guide.
products.bestFor: Buyers who worry about running out of battery mid-clear.
pros: Three 4.0Ah batteries come in the bundle
Brushless motor on a 13 inch clearing width
Weighs about 12 pounds for easier pushing
Premium comfort-grip handle on the shaft
cons: Throw distance is not stated on the listing

products.name: EGO Power+ SNS1200 12 Inch Cordless Snow Shovel

specList.label: Included
specList.value: Tool only; battery and charger sold separately

products.description:
The EGO SNS1200 is a tool-only purchase, and that single fact decides whether it is great or awkward. The listing says the battery and charger are not included. If you already own EGO batteries from a mower or trimmer, you gain a well-regarded snow shovel at the cost of the bare tool. If you do not, you must buy a battery and charger as well.

The tool itself is neat. A 12 inch brushless design throws snow up to 25 feet, a 60-degree directional dial steers the discharge, a speed selector controls throwing distance and a hinged shaft folds for compact storage. With the recommended 2.5Ah ARC lithium battery the listing says it clears a three-car driveway with 6 inches of snow.

Compared with the BAOPROLEI, it has no batteries in the package but a stronger brand platform. Compared with the VOLTASK 48V, it is much smaller and lighter. It costs more than the budget picks in this guide, so it only makes sense if you plan to stay in the EGO battery family.

products.name: Yardzpo 14 Inch Cordless Snow Shovel, 830W Copper Motor
products.description:
The Yardzpo packs a lot of power into a 14 inch body. The listing credits an 830W all-copper motor reaching 16,000 RPM, two batteries with 50+ minutes of runtime and a throw up to 33 feet, which is the longest in this guide. An LED display tracks status, and the adjustable deflector sends snow forward, 45 degrees left or right.

That control is the real benefit, because it lets you place snow beyond the edge of a driveway instead of piling it where you have to move it again. The width suits standard sidewalks and steps, and the tool is described as saving your back and garage space.

Compared with the VOLTASK 48V, it throws farther but clears a narrower, shallower path and does not roll on wheels. Compared with the 24V VOLTASK, it adds a second battery and more reach. It is an easy pick for a household that wants a strong, controllable throw without paying for the largest body.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who want a long, steerable throw and a spare battery.
pros: Throw reaches as far as 33 feet away
Copper motor spins up to 16,000 RPM
Two batteries deliver 50+ minutes
Three discharge directions steer the snow
cons: Narrower and shallower path than the 48V VOLTASK
Does not roll on wheels, so you carry it

products.name: Muylux Brushless Cordless Snow Shovel, 12 Inch
products.description:
The Muylux is the quiet, light option. A 12 inch wide, 6 inch deep path is modest, but a brushless high-torque motor and a lightweight build make it easy to guide around steps and across patios. The listing speaks to seniors and anyone who wants to avoid heavy lifting, with no cords, no gas and no fumes.

That makes it the best fit for someone who finds the other tools too bulky. The cost is that the listing does not publish battery capacity, runtime or throw distance in the text we saw, so you should check the product page and recent feedback.

Compared with the VOLTASK 24V 13 inch, it is a similar scale of tool with fewer numbers to compare. Compared with the EGO, it is a complete package with a battery, but with a less proven name. Choose it if low weight and simplicity are your top concerns.
products.bestFor: Seniors and others who want the lightest possible tool.
pros: Lightweight build suits seniors and tired arms
Brushless motor with a 6 inch clearing depth
No cords, no gas and no exhaust fumes
Rechargeable battery included per the listing
cons: Battery capacity and runtime are not published
Throw distance is not stated on the page

products.name: VOLTASK 24V Cordless Snow Shovel, 13 Inch with Directional Plate
products.description:
This is the lightest tool with a numbered weight in the guide: just 9.3 pounds. A directional plate steers the snow, and an adjustable ergonomic handle with a back-protection design lets you set the grip to your height. The listing says it assembles in minutes and is quiet enough for early mornings.

It is the sensible choice for steps, decks and walkways rather than a long driveway. It lacks some of the extras found on the pricier picks here, and confirming the exact specs and what is included before you buy is wise because bundles vary.

Compared with the Muylux, it publishes real numbers for weight and battery. Compared with the 48V VOLTASK, it is smaller, lighter and cheaper to store, but it cannot match the 16 inch path. It is the easy answer for anyone who wants a competent, compact tool without the bulk.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The footprint of the cut decides how many passes you make and whether the tool copes with heavier snow. The VOLTASK 48V cuts 16 by 8 inches, the Yardzpo 14 inches wide, the BAOPROLEI and VOLTASK 24V 13 inches, and the EGO and Muylux 12 inches. A wider, deeper cut saves time on long driveways. If you only clear steps, width matters little.

Brushless motors run cooler, last longer and waste less battery than brushed motors. The VOLTASK 48V lists 1200W brushless, the Yardzpo an 830W copper motor, and the BAOPROLEI, EGO and Muylux are also brushless. Power helps with wet snow, but it also drains batteries faster. Match the motor to your typical snow.

Without wheels you hold the full weight of the tool as you walk. Wheels roll the weight on pavement. The VOLTASK 48V has wheels and an adjustable support plate, while the others rely on you to carry them. For long driveways, wheels can be the difference between a pleasant clear and a sore back.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Batteries and what is in the box
buyingCriteria.explanation: A snow shovel is only as useful as its battery. The BAOPROLEI ships with three 4.0Ah batteries, the Yardzpo with two, and the EGO ships with none at all. Whether the battery is included is the biggest price trap in this category. Count the total cost of the working kit.

Where the snow lands matters as much as how fast you move it. The Yardzpo throws 33 feet with a three-way discharge, the EGO 25 feet with a 60-degree dial, and the VOLTASK 24V adds a directional plate. A long, steerable throw prevents re-shoveling. If you have nowhere to dump snow, prioritize control.

A heavy tool tires you out, and a bulky tool takes up garage space. The VOLTASK 24V weighs 9.3 pounds, the BAOPROLEI about 12, and the EGO has a hinged shaft for compact storage. The 48V VOLTASK is the biggest. Consider both how it feels in use and where it will live.

howWeEvaluated.title: Clearing performance
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared path width, depth and motor claims. The VOLTASK 48V led with a 16 by 8 inch pass and 1200W brushless motor. The Yardzpo and BAOPROLEI followed, with the 12 inch EGO and Muylux behind.

howWeEvaluated.title: Batteries and kit contents
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted batteries and chargers in each listing. The BAOPROLEI with three packs led, the Yardzpo had two, and the EGO lost points for shipping with no battery. Unlisted details scored neutrally.

howWeEvaluated.title: Throw and control
howWeEvaluated.description: Throw distance and chute adjustment were weighed. The Yardzpo at 33 feet with three discharge directions led, with the EGO's 25 feet and directional dial next. Models with no stated throw lost small points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at weight, wheels and handle design. The VOLTASK 24V at 9.3 pounds and the BAOPROLEI at about 12 pounds scored well for lightness, and the VOLTASK 48V scored well for wheels.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value at this budget
howWeEvaluated.description: Since all six sit under the cap, we weighed capability per dollar of features. The BAOPROLEI leads for batteries, the VOLTASK 48V for capacity and the EGO only for existing platform owners. These are editorial assessments.

faq.q: Is a more expensive electric snow shovel really better?
faq.a: It is stronger in specific ways. The VOLTASK 48V cuts 16 by 8 inches and rolls on wheels, and the BAOPROLEI ships with three batteries. For steps and short paths, the lower-budget models are enough.

faq.q: Why does the EGO cost more than it appears?
faq.a: Because the listing says the battery and charger are not included. If you already own EGO batteries, that is a bargain. If not, add the cost of a battery and charger before comparing it with the others.

faq.q: How many batteries do I need?
faq.a: It depends on the job. The Yardzpo includes two for 50+ minutes, while the BAOPROLEI includes three. For a short walkway, one pack is plenty.
On a long driveway, yes, because you push instead of carrying the weight. The VOLTASK 48V is the only wheeled model here. Shorter jobs do not need them.
Only in shallow passes. Powerful motors help, but wet snow is heavy and drains batteries faster. Clear more often during a storm instead of waiting for deep accumulation.
The VOLTASK 24V listing calls itself quiet, and the Muylux emphasizes no gas or fumes. Most electric shovels are quieter than gas blowers, but none is silent.

faq.q: How do I store the battery in winter?
faq.a: Keep it indoors and charge it before the storm. Cold batteries lose capacity, so bring them in once the job is done. Do not leave them in an unheated shed.
